candidates.title: Push Kuling footwear in NO, FI and DK to close the gap to Sweden
candidates.hypothesis: Shoppers outside Sweden look for children's footwear almost as often as Swedes do, but buy it from low-margin third-party brands (Reima, Viking, Kavat) instead of Kuling. In SE Kuling footwear is 10.8% of revenue and outsells third-party footwear 2:1; in NO it is 5.3% and in FI 4.0%, where third-party footwear outsells Kuling. The products are listed in every market, so this is an exposure and awareness gap, not an assortment gap.
candidates.action: Give Kuling trainers, rubber boots and snow boots the top slots on footwear category and footwear search pages in NO/FI/DK, add a Kuling footwear block to seasonal landing pages and newsletters, and give the Kuling footwear Shopping products their own budget line for the Oct-Dec snow-boot season.

evidence.claim: Oct 2025-Sep 2026, Kuling footwear (3 categories) as share of Babyshop revenue: SE 10.78%, NO 5.32%, FI 4.00%, DK 2.10%; third-party footwear share is similar everywhere (SE 5.38%, NO 6.12%, FI 6.58%). Kuling footwear ladder-consistent GP2: NO 114 374, FI 17 160, DK 7 488 SEK/month.

sizing.baseline_note: Ladder-consistent GP2 of Kuling functional trainers + rubber boots + snow boots in NO (114 374), FI (17 160) and DK (7 488), monthly average Oct 2025-Sep 2026, shop babyshop. GP2 by brand is 'ladder-consistent': agg_daily_kuvio_products.gp1 - shipping_cost - supplement_cost x k, where k per market and period scales product-level supplement_cost down so that brand GP2 sums to agg_daily_profit_ladder.gp2 (k = 0.59-0.81). Raw product-level gp2 is 20-57% below the ladder.
sizing.uplift_rationale: +25% moves NO from 5.3% to ~6.7% of revenue and FI from 4.0% to ~5.0%, i.e. closes about a quarter of the gap to Sweden's 10.8%. High case closes half of the NO gap. Low case is what merchandising slots alone might do without media.

pilot.metric: Kuling footwear revenue as % of FI Babyshop revenue (snow boots + rubber boots + functional trainers)
pilot.control: NO and DK same period, plus FI Q4 2025 share (snow boots 4.75%)
pilot.decision_rule: Roll out to NO/DK if the FI Kuling footwear share rises by at least 1.0 percentage point versus the change in NO over the same weeks, without total FI footwear GP2 falling.

candidates.risks: Part of the uplift cannibalises third-party footwear (5-14% GP2 margin), hence flow_through 0.8. The Swedish position may rest on brand awareness and a Swedish 'best in test' result (138 SE search users for 'best in test') that cannot be copied quickly. FI-specific: SEK/10 pricing may make Kuling boots look expensive next to Reima/Kuoma, and FI base is small (about 130 pairs/month outside Q4), so the pilot must run in snow-boot season. Overlaps with any ads-lens candidate on own-brand budget share.
candidates.curator_note: Brand-level GP2 is rescaled so that brands sum to the profit ladder; the rescale assumes product-level costs are overstated equally for every brand. DK footwear (about 7 500 kr of baseline) is also inside the Danish Kuling item.

candidates.title: Give Kuling more of the Danish shop window
candidates.hypothesis: Danish shoppers arrive looking for Danish brands (27-29% of DK search-page users type one of the big third-party brand names versus 9-13% in SE) and Kuling gets only 28% of product views in DK against 53-58% in SE/FI. When Danes do see Kuling they buy it at least as readily as Swedes, and Kuling carries roughly twice the GP2 margin of the rest of the DK basket, so each point of mix moved to Kuling adds margin.
candidates.action: Rank Kuling first on DK category and generic search pages (regntøj, flyverdragt, termotøj, gummistøvler), add Kuling cross-sell on Konges Sløjd / Wheat / Flöss brand pages, and raise the Kuling share of DK Shopping budget.

sizing.uplift_rationale: Low/base/high = 2 / 5 / 10 points of DK revenue mix moved to Kuling. Ten points would take DK Kuling share to about 30%, still below Norway's 32% twelve-month share. Pure mix shift, no market growth assumed.

candidates.risks: The non-Kuling margin includes Stoy (high margin), so the true third-party margin is lower and the estimate is conservative on margin, but the size of mix shift achievable is a judgement, not a measurement. DK shoppers may be genuinely brand-loyal to Danish labels; pushing Kuling over Konges Sløjd on its own brand pages could cost conversion. Kuling's higher purchase rate per view in DK may reflect self-selection of people who already know the brand.
candidates.curator_note: Kuling's 19.7% share of DK revenue was re-queried by the curator and matches. The size of the mix shift is a judgement, not a measurement.

held_for_stage_two.title: Stop Shopping spend on brands that earn less GP2 than their ad cost
held_for_stage_two.hypothesis: Third-party apparel brands carry 27-43% GP1 but after returns, shipping and handling only about 7-12% GP2, so a brand can look profitable to Google's bidding (conversion value is a profit proxy before those costs) while its entire GP2, including organic sales, is smaller than what is spent advertising it. These brands are not where demand is under-served; the same clicks are worth 3-5x more on Kuling and Stoy.

sizing.baseline_note: Q3-26 monthly Google Shopping spend (agg_daily_kpis_by_gads_product, babyshop + lekmer accounts) on the 71 third-party brand-market pairs flagged on Q2-26 data. Meta catalogue spend on the same brands is not included. GP2 by brand is 'ladder-consistent': agg_daily_kuvio_products.gp1 - shipping_cost - supplement_cost x k, where k per market and period scales product-level supplement_cost down so that brand GP2 sums to agg_daily_profit_ladder.gp2 (k = 0.59-0.81). Raw product-level gp2 is 20-57% below the ladder.
sizing.uplift_rationale: Net GP3 gain as a share of the spend. Total GP2 of these brands is 18% of their Shopping spend, so even if every sale disappeared with the ads the net saving is at least 82% of whatever spend is cut. Base assumes half the spend is removed (0.5 x 0.82); low a quarter, high three quarters.

pilot.metric: FI GP3 (GP2 minus ad spend) and FI Reima revenue
pilot.control: SE/NO/DK same period, where the flagged brands keep their current bidding
pilot.decision_rule: Roll out if FI GP3 is flat or up versus control while Shopping spend on the flagged FI brands falls by at least half; stop if total FI orders fall more than 8% versus control.

held_for_stage_two.risks: The k rescale assumes returns and handling costs are over-stated proportionally for every brand; if third-party returns really are as high as the product table says, the case is stronger, if lower it is weaker. Reima is the anchor brand for Finnish shoppers (22% of FI revenue): cutting its ads may lose baskets that also contain Kuling (FI-specific risk, with low brand reach). Some of these brands are being cleared below cost on purpose; the ads may be serving a stock goal rather than a profit goal. Belongs partly to the paid-media lens - de-duplicate.
